plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds erupt into slender spikes of fragrant violet-blue flowers. They hum with bees and scent the warm early-summer air across sunny hillsides and cottage borders.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer, with peak bloom in June and July in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Mediterranean-climate regions and temperate gardens of Europe, including southern France and England
plants.funFact: Lavender's name probably comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. The Romans used it to scent their baths.

plants.name: Rosa rugosa
plants.description: This tough, sprawling shrub has crinkled leaves and large, clove-scented blooms with silky petals. It thrives on windswept dunes and coastal paths, where flowers open from late spring and keep coming through the summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring through summer, with a strong flush in June
plants.location: Native to the coasts of northeastern Asia, and widely naturalized on the shores of North America and Europe
plants.funFact: After the flowers fade, Rugosa roses form plump, tomato-like red hips. They are especially rich in vitamin C and are used in jams and teas.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: This Australian icon has a crimson flower head the size of a fist, ringed by red bracts. Honeyeaters visit it for its nectar in the bushland around Sydney.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere, mainly September to November
plants.location: Sandstone bushland of New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: What looks like one huge flower is a cluster of hundreds of tiny flowers. The name 'Telopea' comes from a Greek word meaning 'seen from afar'.
